sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) Name the monomer of natural rubber. (b) What is the purpose of vulcanisation?
questions.answer: (a) Isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene). (b) To increase the strength, elasticity and heat resistance of rubber by sulphur cross-links.

questions.q: (a) What are biodegradable polymers? (b) Give one example.
questions.answer: (a) Polymers that are decomposed by microorganisms in the environment. (b) PHBV (or nylon-2-nylon-6).

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Vulcanisation produces an elastomer. (b) Low-density polythene has a linear chain of molecules.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – LDPE has branched chains.

questions.q: Fill in: (a) The salt added to separate soap from the reaction mixture is ______. (b) The by-product of saponification is ______.
questions.answer: (a) sodium chloride (salting out). (b) glycerol.

questions.q: Match: (a) Nylon-6,6 (b) Terylene (c) Bakelite with (i) phenol + HCHO (ii) adipic acid + diamine (iii) ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid.
Write (a) the monomers of buna-S and (b) the type of polymerisation.
questions.answer: (a) 1,3-Butadiene and styrene. (b) Addition (copolymerisation).

questions.q: Name (a) a thermoplastic and (b) a thermosetting polymer.
questions.answer: (a) Polythene (or PVC). (b) Bakelite (or melamine-formaldehyde).

questions.q: State (a) the type of detergent in sodium lauryl sulphate and (b) one use of cationic detergents.
questions.answer: (a) Anionic detergent. (b) As germicides/in hair conditioners.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is butyl rubber? State one of its properties and use.
questions.answer: A copolymer of isobutylene with about 2% isoprene; it is impermeable to air and is used for tyre inner tubes.

questions.q: Differentiate between natural rubber and vulcanised rubber.
questions.answer: Natural rubber is soft, sticky and weak, with cis-polyisoprene chains; vulcanised rubber is heated with sulphur, which cross-links the chains, giving hardness, elasticity and resistance to heat and solvents.

questions.q: What are biodegradable polymers? Give an example and a use.
questions.answer: Polymers broken down by bacteria into harmless products. PHBV, used in packaging, orthopaedic devices and controlled release of drugs.

questions.q: What is a micelle? How does soap clean?
questions.answer: An aggregate of soap molecules in water with the hydrocarbon tails inward and ionic heads outward. Grease enters the hydrophobic core and gets emulsified, to be washed away with water.

questions.q: Why are detergents more effective than soaps in hard water?
questions.answer: Soaps form insoluble calcium and magnesium salts (scum) with hard water; the Ca and Mg salts of synthetic detergents are soluble, so they continue to lather.

questions.q: Give the difference between addition and condensation polymers with an example.
questions.answer: Addition polymers are formed from unsaturated monomers without loss of any small molecule (polythene); condensation polymers are formed by joining bifunctional monomers with the loss of small molecules such as water (nylon-6,6).

questions.q: Write the monomer and structure of teflon.
questions.answer: Tetrafluoroethene, F2C=CF2; polymer –(CF2–CF2)n–, used for non-stick cookware.

questions.q: Why are branched-chain detergents harmful?
questions.answer: They are not decomposed by bacteria (non-biodegradable) and cause persistent foam and pollution of water bodies.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the cleansing action of soap and the formation of micelles.
questions.answer: Soap has a hydrophilic carboxylate head and a long hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail. In water the tails collect around the grease with heads facing the water, forming micelles; grease is suspended in water as an emulsion and rinsed away.

questions.q: Write the preparation of nylon-6,6 and terylene with their uses.
questions.answer: Nylon-6,6: hexamethylenediamine + adipic acid, condensation polymerisation by heating at 553 K under pressure; used in fibres, ropes and bristles. Terylene: ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid at 420–460 K with Zn(OAc)2/Sb2O3; used for fabrics and sails.

questions.q: How is natural rubber vulcanised? Explain how the properties improve.
questions.answer: Natural rubber (cis-polyisoprene) is heated with 3–5% sulphur at 373–415 K, forming disulphide cross-links between chains; it becomes stronger, more elastic, less sticky, and resistant to heat, abrasion and chemicals.

questions.q: Distinguish between thermoplastic and thermosetting polymers with examples.
questions.answer: Thermoplastics soften on heating and harden on cooling and can be remoulded (polythene, PVC); thermosetting polymers get permanently hard on heating due to cross-linking and cannot be reshaped (bakelite, melamine).

questions.q: Compare the low-density and high-density polythene in preparation, structure and use.
questions.answer: LDPE: free-radical polymerisation of ethene at high pressure (1000–2000 atm) with traces of O2 or peroxide; branched chains; soft, used in films and squeeze bottles. HDPE: Ziegler–Natta catalyst at 6–7 atm, 333–343 K; linear chains; hard, used for buckets and toys.

questions.q: Explain the types of synthetic detergents with examples.
questions.answer: Anionic: sodium alkylbenzene sulphonate (washing powders); cationic: cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (hair conditioners, germicide); non-ionic: polyethylene glycol stearate (liquid dishwashing).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) What is butyl rubber? (b) How does vulcanisation modify natural rubber? (c) Name two uses of rubber.
questions.answer:
(a) A synthetic rubber formed by copolymerisation of isobutylene with a small amount of isoprene; it has very low permeability to air and is used for tyre tubes.
(b) Natural rubber is heated with sulphur, which forms cross-links between the isoprene chains; the product is harder, elastic, resists temperature and wear.
(c) Tyres, belts, footwear and gloves.

questions.q: (a) What are biodegradable polymers? Describe PHBV and nylon-2-nylon-6. (b) Why is the disposal of synthetic polymers a problem?
questions.answer:
(a) Polymers degraded by microorganisms. PHBV is a copolymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic and 3-hydroxypentanoic acids, used in packaging and as drug carriers; nylon-2-nylon-6 is an alternating polyamide of glycine and 6-aminohexanoic acid.
(b) Synthetic polymers such as polythene and PVC are non-biodegradable, persist for years, choke drains and harm animals; burning produces toxic gases.

questions.q: (a) Classify polymers on the basis of their source and structure with examples. (b) Give the preparation of polythene (LDPE and HDPE), PVC and Teflon.
questions.answer:
(a) Natural (cellulose, proteins, rubber), semi-synthetic (rayon) and synthetic (nylon, polythene); linear (HDPE), branched (LDPE) and cross-linked (bakelite).
(b) LDPE: ethene at high pressure with a trace of O2; HDPE: Ziegler–Natta catalyst (TiCl4 + Al(C2H5)3) at low pressure; PVC: free-radical polymerisation of CH2=CHCl; Teflon: F2C=CF2 with persulphate at high pressure.

questions.q: (a) How is soap manufactured? Write the saponification reaction. (b) Compare soaps and synthetic detergents.
questions.answer:
(a) Fat (triglyceride) is boiled with NaOH: (RCOO)3C3H5 + 3NaOH → 3RCOONa + C3H5(OH)3; soap is separated by adding salt and moulded.
(b) Soaps are salts of fatty acids, biodegradable, ineffective in hard water and acidic medium; detergents are sulphonates or sulphates, effective in hard water, work in acidic media, and branched ones are non-biodegradable.
